title: The world: ten stadiums on one continent, ten captains

status_vocabulary.accepted: Jack answered; the selected option and scope are recorded

brief: Jack, 2026-09-24: expand to 10 stadiums that make up a continent, each in the region that fits it (ice in a cold place, one in a volcano, one on a tropical island), selectable from the menu; define hazards, night lights and other defining features per stadium; grow to 10 captains, each assigned a field; one field is a tropical beach.

decisions.question: When does building start?

options.label: Plan now, build after #346
options.tradeoff: Nothing is built until Jack passes the Exhibition gate (#346). Safest for focus; the world waits.

options.label: Plan now; rails and greyboxes now; art after #346
options.tradeoff: The data rails, the new captains in data, the four new park files, new hazard patterns, greyboxes and the map picker are built now. No park art. Changes one AGENTS.md line: extra parks move from 'do not start' to 'greybox only'.

options.label: Build everything now
options.tradeoff: Parks and art become products now. Conflicts with AGENTS.md, #37 and FD-17.

decisions.existing_contract: AGENTS.md 'Do not start: extra parks as products (#37)'; FD-01 (rails and greyboxes allowed); FD-17 (greybox sitting before art).
decisions.acceptance: One scope line in AGENTS.md an agent can obey without asking.
decisions.accepted_scope: Plan now. Build now: the world data rail, the new captains in data, the four new park files, the new hazard patterns, the greyboxes and the map picker. No park, backdrop or map art until Jack passes #346; a park's art still waits for its greybox sitting (FD-17, WD-02 open). AGENTS.md carries the scope line.

decision_evidence.question: WD-01: A plan now, build after #346 / B rails and greyboxes now, art after #346 / C everything now

decisions.question: In what order does park art come?

options.label: Keep FD-17
options.tradeoff: All ten as greyboxes first; Jack sits each greybox; then art one park at a time.

options.label: Art as each new park is built
options.tradeoff: Faster to look good; risks art on a park whose play is not settled.

decisions.existing_contract: FD-17 (greybox sitting before art, one park in art at a time).
decisions.acceptance: The art order written in the plan.
decisions.accepted_scope: Keep FD-17: all ten parks are greyboxes first; Jack sits each greybox; then art one park at a time.

decision_evidence.question: WD-02: A Keep FD-17 / B Art as each new park is built

decisions.question: Do backdrops come back?

options.label: Blender kit art per park
options.tradeoff: The region past the fence is authored art (the volcano, the sea). Behind WD-02.

options.label: Data greybox backdrops now, art later
options.tradeoff: A backdrop row per region: a silhouette shape and a palette, drawn by one builder for every park. Reads as a place at greybox stage.

options.label: No backdrops
options.tradeoff: The field stays in an empty sky until art.

decisions.existing_contract: FD-16-R2 (the hand-built backdrops were deleted; identity returns only as art). B is a data rail, not per-park Unity art.
decisions.acceptance: A park's backdrop is named by its kit row and drawn by one builder; no park id in code.
decisions.accepted_scope: Backdrops come back as Blender kit pieces, one per park, in tools/blender (a kit slot, not Unity-only art). A rough blockout is enough; finished art is not required (Jack). Reading recorded for confirmation: a rough blockout backdrop counts as greybox and may be built with the park's greybox (C5); finishing it waits for #346 and the park's sitting (WD-01, WD-02).

decision_evidence.question: WD-03: A Blender kit art per park / B Data greybox backdrops now, art later / C No backdrops

decisions.question: How many hazards does a park have?

options.label: One primary hazard plus one night change
options.tradeoff: The parks.md rule. Each park has one thing to learn by day and one thing that changes at night.

options.label: Two hazards per park
options.tradeoff: More variety; harder to read at gameplay distance and to teach.

decisions.acceptance: Each park sheet names one day hazard and one night change.
decisions.accepted_scope: One primary hazard per park plus one night change.

decisions.question: Which new hazard patterns are built?

options.label: All three, one child each
options.tradeoff: Surge (the tide), drifting redirect (dust devils), fog bank (Stillwater). Each is a closed-library row with its own tests; none awards a result (FD-08).

options.label: Only what the existing patterns can do
options.tradeoff: The new parks reuse status volumes, redirects, solid bodies and timed movers.

options.label: A and B mixed
options.tradeoff: Build surge and drifting redirect; give Stillwater an existing pattern instead of fog.

decisions.recommendation: C. Fog as a vision effect hides the ball from a human and not from the CPU (FD-14: the CPU reads the park), which is unfair. Stillwater's hazard becomes floating lily pads (solid bodies on a timed drift) unless Jack wants fog as look only.
decisions.existing_contract: FD-08 (a hazard may be random, never decides a result); FD-09 (closed pattern library); FD-14 (CPU reads the park); FD-19 (off the base paths).
decisions.acceptance: Every new type has a row naming its pattern; a scenario per pattern shows the ball and bodies still decide the play.
decisions.accepted_scope: Build two new patterns, surge (the tide) and drifting redirect (dust devils), plus the Summit wind schedule as an environment row; Stillwater reuses existing patterns (drifting lily pads). No fog hazard.

decisions.question: What are night lights?

options.label: A themed light rig per park, plus its night look

options.label: Night look rows only
options.tradeoff: No light props; only the sky and light change.

options.label: Night also changes the light you play in
options.tradeoff: For example a darker outfield. Reopens FD-11-R2.

decisions.recommendation: A. The rig is a kit slot (the 'night' slot) filled per park, greybox first (a data row: pole count, height, lamp color).
decisions.existing_contract: FD-11-R2 (lights stay on; night changes only the view outside and the hazards).
decisions.acceptance: Every park names a night rig; the field is lit the same at every park.
decisions.accepted_scope: Each park gets a themed night light rig (a kit slot, greybox row first) and its night look row; the play light stays the same (FD-11-R2 holds).

options.tradeoff: Kai becomes a river rider on the delta (faction renamed from Tide Riders); stats and Wave Swing stay.

options.tradeoff: A new captain who belongs in a marsh (working idea: a long-legged frog jumper, speed and range) founds Stillwater Marsh's faction. Kai is dropped, or returns later as a role player on Fenn's beach team.
